text:
[LERR.8.1] **The number is the identity; the name is a label.** A
conforming implementation must use these numbers to mean these things. It
is **not** obliged to use these spellings, and generally should not: an
implementation picks names that suit its own language's conventions.
`DS_ERR_INVAL` is what this implementation calls `-1`, not what `-1` is.

This is why the registry is a protobuf enum. Enum semantics already say
exactly that — the value is what travels, the identifier is a convenience
of the generated binding — so the notation states the rule rather than
describing it ([STYL.2.15]).

It also buys enforcement that four prose registers could not manage between
them. `protoc` refuses a value defined twice, and refuses a `reserved`
value reused. Neither failure is visible to any gate, because a dictionary written in prose
has nothing to check it.
